problem_trigger: The first issue #128 decision-product assignment produced multiple overlapping producer/controller handoffs (#143, #144, #145, #147). Independent C live-state premise checking caught stale duplicate-state assumptions before integration; duplicate PR #147 appeared even after #143 had been corrected and C-reviewed.
prior_design: DH0004 added producer branch/SHA visibility to prevent missing-work misdiagnosis, but the controller still lacked a sufficiently simple rule for selecting one authoritative handoff when the same assignment generated multiple live PRs/branches.
hypothesis_rationale: Treating assignment identity plus ancestry/content as the durable unit of work, selecting one authoritative continuation, immediately closing superseded duplicates, and withholding replacement production until disposition should preserve producer work while reducing duplicate verification and controller toil.
exact_change: Within ordinary management authority, D reconciled the issue #128 producer evidence, retained PR #143 exact corrected head c6f0924ba10d29f0a5de31e1055892951af18885 as the authoritative candidate, closed later duplicate PR #147 unmerged, accepted independent C PASS on that exact head after successful CI, integrated PR #143 as main 12b398abf7b066e82091926451372316933cc441, and closed stale controller PR #146 rather than merging obsolete pre-integration state. No scheduler, permission, governance, security, licensing, or constitutional authority changed.
expected_benefit: Prevent duplicate producer handoffs from consuming C/D capacity.
Preserve corrected producer work rather than restarting it.
Keep controller state aligned to one exact branch/SHA/PR per active assignment.
Reduce stale bookkeeping commits between final C PASS and integration.
risks: Ancestry-based continuation selection can be wrong if parallel branches contain genuinely distinct higher-value corrections.
Aggressive duplicate closure can hide useful alternatives unless content and task identity are checked first.
Repeated reconciliation can become toil if producers continue creating parallel handoffs.
evaluation_window: Next 6-12 healthy controller cycles and the next two Tier-2 producer handoffs.
evaluation_criteria: At most one authoritative live PR is retained per Tier-2 assignment unless D documents a higher-EV exception.
No producer-ready work is discarded solely because a duplicate exists; ancestry/content/task identity are checked.
Duplicate/stale handoff cleanup does not consume roughly half of controller capacity across three windows.
Final exact-head C PASS is followed by prompt D disposition without nonessential main mutations.

observed_outcomes.observation: C PASSed PR #143 exact head c6f0924ba10d29f0a5de31e1055892951af18885 after its earlier QUALIFY was corrected.
PR #147 duplicated the same assignment on a separate A branch and had no C review; D closed it without redoing research.
PR #143 exact head had successful Validate HumanityAI run 34968687518, was current with main, and D integrated it as main 12b398abf7b066e82091926451372316933cc441.

Producer visibility solved the missing-work failure but exposed a second failure mode: visibility without authoritative-handoff selection can surface duplicate candidates. The next control should be simplification, not another coordination layer.

failures_side_effects: Multiple PRs for one assignment consumed producer, verifier, and controller attention.
A stale controller reconciliation PR (#146) became obsolete before it could safely be canonicalized.
lessons: Track one authoritative branch/SHA/PR per assignment after checking ancestry, content, and task identity.
Close superseded duplicates promptly but preserve their branches/SHAs as historical evidence.
Do not merge stale controller bookkeeping after the underlying Tier-2 disposition has changed.
After final exact-head C PASS and green CI, prioritize disposition before nonessential controller mutations.
